subdomain: 2.5 Implement prompt reuse strategies (caching, modular prompts, Skills)

en.question: A custom inspection-report Skill works in Claude Code. Its helper downloads calibration tables and installs a Python package at runtime. The team wants to reuse it in the Claude API and claude.ai. Under the runtime and cross-surface constraints documented in the cited Skills overview, which decisions belong in the promotion plan? Select 3 answers.

options.text: Distribute and track the intended Skill version separately on each surface rather than assuming automatic synchronization.
options.note: Custom Skills do not automatically sync among Claude Code, the API, and claude.ai. Deliberate per-surface distribution is needed to keep the intended content available.

options.text: Enable the API's required code execution environment and redesign the helper around its available dependencies and lack of runtime network access.
options.note: The cited API Skills environment requires code execution and cannot download tables or install packages at runtime. Inputs or preprocessing must be supplied through a supported path rather than inherited from Claude Code's environment.

options.text: Use the successful Claude Code execution as certification that network access, package installation, and sharing behave identically on all surfaces.
options.note: The surfaces have different runtime and sharing constraints. Success in the local environment does not establish API or claude.ai compatibility.

options.text: Audit the instructions, scripts, and referenced resources, and restrict the tools and data available to the Skill.
options.note: A Skill carries instructions and potentially executable code, so it requires software-like trust review. Packaging procedural knowledge does not create an independent permission boundary.
